**Finding submitted: deviation (RENEWAL, medium severity)**

**What the document says.** Term mechanics sit in paragraph 4(a) (p0016). The Initial Term is one year and the Agreement "will automatically renew for additional 1-year terms." No party may terminate during the Initial Term (except for breach), and thereafter "Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party."

**Analysis.**
- Renewal term length: 12 months — acceptable, and not the automatic multi-year renewal that would be walk-away territory.
- Exit window: there is no separate non-renewal notice provision, so the 90-day for-convenience right is our only route out of a renewal. 90 days exceeds the fallback ceiling of 60 days, which is a material failure of the fallback — hence a deviation rather than a fallback-compliant clause.
- Price uplift: no renewal price-increase language exists, because Kubient is paid out of auction fees rather than a Customer subscription fee, so the CPI/3% cap has nothing to attach to.
- No Vendor renewal reminder — noted in the rationale only, as a minor sub-element rather than a separate deviation.

**Redline (validated ok:true).** I split the bilateral notice period rather than shortening it for both sides: Customer moves to 30 days (the preferred position), while Kubient stays at 90 days. Accelerating the Vendor's own exit right would work against us, so the edit is confined to the side that binds us.
